name: Abigail
bio:
Abigail was the wife of Nabal of the clan of Caleb — intelligent and beautiful, married to a harsh and foolish man. Her composed, wise intervention to avert a massacre makes her one of the most admired women in the Old Testament, and she later became David's wife.

After Nabal rudely rejected David's request for help, David furiously vowed to wipe out his whole household; a servant told Abigail what had happened, and she quickly prepared a large gift of bread, wine, dressed meat, roasted grain, raisin cakes, and fig cakes, loaded it on donkeys, and set out to meet David without telling her husband (1 Samuel 25:14-19).

Abigail bowed before David and pleaded earnestly for her husband's rudeness, urging him not to take vengeance with his own hands: "Since the LORD has kept you, my lord, from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hands... please remember your servant." She also prophesied that the LORD would surely make David a lasting dynasty, and that he would be spared the anguish of needless bloodshed on his conscience (1 Samuel 25:23-31). David praised the LORD for sending her and blessed her discernment, saying, "Blessed be your good judgment and blessed be you, who have kept me from bloodshed this day and from avenging myself with my own hands," accepting her gift and agreeing to spare Nabal's household (1 Samuel 25:32-35).

When Abigail returned home, she found Nabal drunk and waited until the next morning to tell him what had happened; he was so stricken with shock that his heart failed, and about ten days later he died. On hearing the news, David sent for Abigail to become his wife; she bowed to the ground and humbly replied she was ready to be a servant to wash the feet of David's servants, then rose and went with his messengers to become his wife (1 Samuel 25:36-42). Abigail's composure, eloquence, and wisdom not only saved her entire household but also kept David from a grave act of vengeance he would have regretted, making her story one of Scripture's finest examples of defusing conflict through gentleness and wisdom.

When David returned from marching with Achish, he found Ziklag burned and Abigail and Ahinoam taken captive by Amalekite raiders; David inquired of the LORD, pursued the raiders, and recovered both his wives along with everything else that had been taken (1 Samuel 30:1-19).
